## QUESTION 1

1. __Convert values to missing__ Start with a fresh copy of the flights dataset by reading it in from the link provided above (as opposed to starting with the dataset you ended with in the last assignment). Identify data values that are problematic, non-sense or impossible and change them to be missing. In your report include one record example (one row) from your clean data, in the raw JSON format. Your example should display at least one missing value so that we can verify it was done correctly. (Note: JSON will convert NaN's to null). Describe your process for finding values that needed to be changed, and how you changed them.

Checking which columns needed to have values replaced was a combination of printing known problem rows, and looking through the visual representation of the database in DataWrangler. I found columns that had values like n/a, 1500+, or -999 and replaced them with null.

```{python}
# check = df.group_by('month').len().sort('month')
# check = df.group_by('num_of_delays_carrier').len().sort('num_of_delays_carrier')
# check = df.group_by('num_of_delays_late_aircraft').len().sort('num_of_delays_late_aircraft')
# check = df.group_by('minutes_delayed_nas').len().sort('minutes_delayed_nas')
# check
```

```{python}
# Find and replace problem values in certain columns with null values
missing_df = df.with_columns(
  pl.col('month')
    .replace('n/a', None),
  pl.col('num_of_delays_carrier')
    .replace('1500+', None)
    .cast(pl.Int64),
  pl.col('num_of_delays_late_aircraft')
    .replace(-999, None),
  pl.col('minutes_delayed_nas')
    .replace(-999, None)
)

one_row = missing_df.head(1).to_dicts()
print(json.dumps(one_row))
```

## QUESTION 2

2. __Filling in missing data__ For all the "minutes_delayed" columns, fill in any missing values with the median of that column. For the "num_of" columns, fill in missing values with that column's mean.

_Nothing to write/report for this question_

```{python}
# Fill num_of columns with mean, and minutes delayed columns with median
filled_data = missing_df.with_columns(
  pl.col('^num_of_.*$').fill_null(strategy = 'mean'),
  pl.col('^minutes_delayed_.*$').fill_null(pl.col('^minutes_delayed_.*$').median())
)
filled_data.head()
```

The distribution of delays by carrier is more evenly spread, with a clear peak around 400 delays, and a large spike at 696. It's slightly right skewed.

